items.title: Cursor adds ability to build and share live apps
facts: Agents have lowered the cost of writing code, but most apps and tools that users build never make it off of localhost.
Now, you can build live apps directly in Cursor and share them with a link.
Describe what you want to create and Cursor will handle the rest: build the app, set up a database, configure auth, and deploy it.

items.title: OpenAI introduces GPT-6 Cyber for security research
facts: We’re introducing GPT‑6 Cyber, a major leap in security research: more capable at finding and fixing vulnerabilities, and far more reliable staying within the boundaries researchers set.
On ExploitGym, which tests whether models can exploit a specified vulnerability, GPT‑6 Cyber scores 48.5%, up from 32.1% for GPT‑5.6 Cyber.
Our researchers used GPT‑6 Cyber to develop 948 privilege escalation exploits in Linux and identify 81 previously unknown high-severity vulnerabilities in Firefox.

x_posts.author: @OpenAI
x_posts.text:
Introducing GPT‑6 Cyber: a major advance in security research that pairs stronger capabilities with better model alignment.

The model powered the Linux kernel research we announced yesterday, and security teams at companies like Mozilla, Palo Alto Networks, Calif, and Cisco—alongside our own at OpenAI—are already putting it to work.

GPT-6 Cyber is available to select Daybreak Red customers and we are expanding access over time.

https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-cyber/

items.title: Crush v0.100.0 adds subagents, Sysadmin Mode and PGP/SSH prompts
facts: Crush can now run a team of subagents, permissions are much more flexible, and you can now do GPG and SSH auth right inside Crush.
Crush can now spawn a little team of friendly subagents in the background, as well as check on them, send them mid-run follow-ups, stop them, or move them to a different model.

x_posts.author: @0x_peuq
x_posts.text:
GPT-6 Cyber is here, positioned as the strongest model for security work

-> 48.5% on ExploitGym, a new record for the benchmark
-> Found 81 previously unknown high-severity vulnerabilities in Firefox
-> Showed how 948 Linux bugs could be chained by attackers for privilege escalation
-> Access limited to Daybreak Red participants via Codex and the API

Meanwhile the expected GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol did not ship today. Waiting on tomorrow

items.title: Kiro launches Teams credit pooling for shared AI credits
facts: Enterprise administrators can now share Kiro credits across seated users with credit pooling.
Each seat costs $20 per month and adds 500 monthly credits to one shared pool, so credits one user doesn't use stay available to the rest of the team.

items.title: Claude Code optimizes background subagent status updates to cut usage
facts: Background subagents in Claude Code now use less of your usage limit.

A running subagent updates its status line every 30 seconds, and each update used to re-read its whole conversation. Now Haiku 5.5 writes it from short notes instead, so each update costs about 99% less.

items.title: Hot tips on reducing Codex credit usage in planning workflows
facts: This makes a pretty damn big difference in usage when coding using Codex.

I suggest adding this to the Codex chat as soon as you create it as a persistent rule as well as adding another rule stating that any prompts in the middle of doing work are meant to be used as additional information or changes and previous work should be continued while adding the new work to that list, unless told otherwise.
